The protection routes above start at the address bus rather than at AS_n, because the protection decode has to settle before the strobe-qualified path it gates. Section 8 sets that requirement against the 20 ns the processor holds the address valid ahead of AS_n.

Each broad address range above reports its longest input route. For example, an A20..A18 change reaches ROM_ALIAS_n through the 45 ns select path of U_LOW128, while an A23..A21 change first passes through U_PRIMARY and then uses the 42 ns enable path of U_LOW128.

Timing Boundary

The totals above end at the motherboard request outputs or begin at a subsystem completion input. Each subsystem document adds its local decode, device access time, and completion generation. Every adapter must keep its full response below the 51.1 microsecond minimum timeout boundary.

For the acknowledgement-release direction the constraint is the MC68EC000FN10 limit of 110 ns from AS_n or the data strobes negating to /DTACK negating. The shared motherboard contribution is the 17.2 ns FAST release tree (SN74F21 + SN74F21 + SN74F32, all low-to-high). This is logic delay only and does not on its own prove the CPU-pin timing: each subsystem adds its own local release-qualification logic ahead of its completion output, and PCB trace, connector, and receiver loading delay must be added. Those are resolved on the subsystem pages and in the final board timing review.

Measure each complete release path on the assembled board at the CPU pin. The pass limit is 110 ns from AS_n or both data strobes negating to DTACK_n high. The DRAM path has 28.5 ns of verified logic delay and an 81.5 ns allowance for receiver, interconnect, and loading; see DRAM release timing.

The firmware chip select takes at most 237 ns from the address path or 282 ns from the function-code qualification path. The AT28C256 then needs as much as 150 ns to produce valid data. The firmware interface therefore supplies the required wait states instead of acknowledging the cycle directly from ROM_CYCLE_n.

These calculations use the SN74HCT -40 C to +85 C values and a 50 pF test load, except the SN74F21 and SN74F32 release-tree stages, which use the 0 C to +70 C SN74F N-package limits (see the FAST-family temperature note in section 26). Section 26 also defines how socket, trace, and receiver capacitance are checked when each subsystem schematic is completed.

26. Electrical Compatibility and Fanout

This section verifies logic levels and static-current fanout within the address-decode network. It does not include memory, peripheral, expansion, connector, or PCB trace loading.

Verification Rules

HIGH noise margin = VOH(min) - VIH(min)
LOW noise margin  = VIL(max) - VOL(max)

A connection is statically compatible when both margins are zero or greater. Fanout is checked by comparing the sum of receiver input currents with the output current at which the driver guarantees its stated VOH or VOL.

The binding FAST current is the 0.6 mA LOW input current (IIL) that each SN74F input can pull from its driver. No net in the acknowledgement tree presents more than one FAST load to an SN74F21 or SN74F32 output, and each of those outputs sinks 20 mA, so the sink ratio never falls below about 33. U_PROT loads nothing heavily: its inputs draw 100 uA at worst and its outputs sink 24 mA. AS_n, UDS_n, and LDS_n gain FAST loads at U_DRAM_DTACK_GATE; that budget is on the DRAM page because those strobes are decoded there.

FAST-Family Temperature Range

The N-package SN74F10, SN74F21, and SN74F32 are characterized only over TA = 0 C to +70 C. This is the motherboard's specified operating range because the design requires plastic through-hole FAST parts. The HCT devices have wider published ranges, but that does not widen the assembled motherboard rating.

NORMAL_MISC_n 1 10 pF HCT timing characterized at 50 pF 40 pF remains for socket, trace, and probe loading
ROM_CYCLE_n 2 20 pF HCT timing characterized at 50 pF 30 pF remains for socket, trace, and probe loading

The capacitance totals use the 10 pF maximum for each HCT input and 6 pF for a MACH210 input. They exclude package sockets, traces, vias, connectors, and measurement probes. NORMAL_EXP_n carries four loads and has the least remaining margin among the HCT nets. Keep each completed HCT net at or below 50 pF, or add another HCT buffer and recalculate its timing.

Revision 2.1 keeps processor R/W within the 100 pF design budget. The expansion interface replaces six direct loads with two inputs on U_EXP_RW_BUF, and the IDE interface adds one input on its local two-inverter direction buffer. The result is nine loads and about 86 pF against the processor's 130 pF limit. The page unit avoids two more: U_PAGE_MMU drives XCVR_DIR to its two transceivers rather than letting them sit on R/W, as Paging records. That leaves 14 pF below the 100 pF design budget and 44 pF below the processor limit for trace, socket, and probe loading. The board audit must measure the completed net.

Each of A16..A1 also gains two HCT244 inputs from the expansion interface, for at most 20 pF added receiver capacitance and 2 uA added leakage per line. Add these to the line's device-specific consumers when checking the complete motherboard.

The IDE interface adds one HCT244 input to A1..A3, one PAL input to A4, one PAL input to each data strobe, and one HCT04 input to R/W. Its HCT244 output feeds the remaining low address decode, so the PAL does not add a second processor load to A1..A3. The IDE page records that boundary.

The SN74F10, SN74F21, and SN74F32 data sheets state no input capacitance. The FAST acknowledgement nets each carry one FAST load and a short motherboard trace, so they stay well inside the 50 pF, 500 ohm switching-test load; the exact receiver plus trace figure is confirmed in the final board load audit alongside the HCT nets.

Loading rules for the remaining subsystem schematics

CPU outputs Keep total direct loading at or below 100 pF. This leaves 30 pF below the processor's 130 pF limit for board and measurement loading. Each device page and the final motherboard load audit. Revision 2.1 gives R/W about 14 pF of margin to this design limit before board and probe loading.
HCT outputs Keep total loading at or below the 50 pF timing condition. Add an HCT buffer if a net exceeds it. The page that owns the driven receivers.

28. DMA Bus Integration

The shared address, data, function-code, and control nets are master-neutral. OWN_n selects the MC68450 address latches and qualifies its register chip select. A new ACT244 control buffer keeps each master's direct R/W, AS, UDS, LDS, and FC load below the former fanout limit. Two ACT373 latches and three HCT245 transceivers implement the manual's multiplex circuit. See DMA Controller for pins, polarity, and lane crossing. 

CPU_BERR_n      = BUS_BERR_n OR (NOT OWN_n)
DMA_FAULT_SET_n = BUS_BERR_n OR BGACK_n
DMAC_CS_n       = IO12_n OR (NOT OWN_n) OR (UDS_n AND LDS_n)
DMA_BERR        = (A23 OR A22) AND (NOT OWN_n) AND (NOT AS_n)

DTACK_GROUP3_n = IDE_DTACK_n AND DMAC_DTACK_n AND BSRAM_DTACK_n AND 1
DTACK_RAW_n    = GROUP0_n AND GROUP1_n AND GROUP2_n AND GROUP3_n

An SN74HCT125N isolates the bidirectional DMAC DTACK pin. The CPU-side output is DMAC_DTACK_RAW_n. The two-stage arm and raw-strobe qualifier in DMA section 8 produces DMAC_DTACK_n for the completion tree; do not feed the isolated raw output into the tree. One gate carries motherboard completion into the DMAC only while OWN is low; another carries register completion into group 3 only while OWN is high. Pull-ups define both isolated nodes. The timeout counter resets on every AS-high interval, so a long DMA ownership burst does not accumulate one timeout across several bus cycles.

Five interlocks bound where a DMA cycle can reach. U_DMA_QUAL adds OWN_ACTIVE to the protected and expansion normal-cycle qualifiers, so the CL-GD5428 window, the top I/O region, and all four expansion memory windows stop qualifying. Both I/O decoders take an ownership enable as well. The boot-ROM alias takes the same term, so the MC68450 always sees DRAM in the low 128 KiB, and the page unit closes its aperture. U_PROT then asserts DMA_BERR for any DMA address at or above $400000, which aborts the channel instead of leaving it to the bus timeout. Main memory is the only region a DMA cycle can reach. The firmware ROM is the only thing outside it that will still answer, and ROM is read-only, so the worst case there is a discarded write on a channel that is aborting anyway.

BUS_BERR is retained only after BGACK proves DMA ownership. It masks completion and drives BEC code 101 for at least two DMA clocks. Reset drives BEC code 000 regardless of ownership. This covers the A84G ownership restriction and prevents a CPU fault from parking the DMAC. DMAC DMA_BR_n, BGACK, and OWN use 2.2 kohm pull-ups; their calculated 2.0 V threshold crossing is below 45 ns at 50 pF. Final rise time, control buffer loading, and all twelve relative clock phases remain post-layout scope checks.

BIOS Backup SRAM Integration

Route qualified IO13_n from U_IO_HIGH pin 10 to the backup SRAM qualifier. Connect bus A1..A15 and D0..D7, shared AS_n, LDS_n, UDS_n, R_W, and RESET_n as listed there. The existing region-7 protection and I/O ownership enables exclude user, CPU-space, and DMA requests.

The SRAM accepts a supervisor lower-byte read or write and supplies BSRAM_DTACK_n after its clocked delay. Wire that signal to U_DTACK_C pin 4. Retain the timeout mask and CPU/DMA completion isolation. Update both group-3 equations and physical gate ties together; do not connect SRAM /CEO to the completion tree.

For the loading audit, add 6 pF/1 uA to each A1..A15 net and 8 pF/1 uA to each D0..D7 net. Add one CMOS input to IO13_n, UDS_n, and RESET_n, and two to each AS_n, LDS_n, and R_W net. Check the SRAM's 2.1 mA low and 1 mA high data-output drive against the total shared-bus load. U_BSRAM_CLK_BUF replaces the startup-divider load on DRAM_CLK_10; it supplies separate BSRAM_CLK and STARTUP_CLK_10 branches.
